p4.title: Markets
p4.text: A market is a place __(0)__ people buy food. Most markets are __(1)__ the street, and they are open one or two days a week. You can find fruit, vegetables, bread, clothes and toys __(2)__ a market. The fruit often comes from farms near the town, so it __(3)__ very good. parts.text: Bill's grandfather had a small farm outside the town. Every Saturday he took his vegetables to the market. Bill helped him because he wasn't at school on Saturdays. Their potatoes were the best in the village.

parts.text: One Saturday morning it was very windy. Bill put a big bag of potatoes on the table, but the bag was old and it broke. All the potatoes fell and went down the street! Bill ran after them.

differences: In your picture there are five oranges, but in my picture there are three.
In your picture the bag is on the table, but in my picture it is under the table.
In your picture the boy is drinking, but in my picture he is eating.
In your picture the dog is black, but in my picture it is white.
In your picture there are flowers next to the box, but in my picture there is bread.

p2.title: Sally goes shopping
p2.examiner_open: These pictures show a story. It's called 'Sally goes shopping'. Look at the pictures first. Sally's mother tells her what to buy and gives her a bag, and Sally goes to the market. Now you tell the story.
frames: Sally's mother tells her to buy apples, bread and cheese. Sally takes a bag and goes out.
At the market Sally buys apples, bread and cheese. The woman at the table helps her.
Sally is walking home, but the bag is old and it breaks. All the apples fall in the street.
A man helps Sally to pick up the apples. He gives her a new bag and Sally says thank you.

sets.reason: A carrot is a vegetable. The others are fruit.
You don't take a cloud to the market. It's in the sky.
You can't eat a shoe. You wear it.
You can't buy things in a river. It's in the countryside.

p1: Part One. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Look, Grandpa. This is the market in our street on Saturday morning.
It's very busy! Who's the girl with the big red apple?
That's Sally. She always buys the biggest apple.
Can you see the line? This is an example. Now you listen and draw lines.
Who's that boy? He's carrying a big box.
That's Peter. The box is full of potatoes and it's very heavy.
And the woman with the bread and the cakes?
She's Anna. Her bread is the best in the town. We buy it every week.
Can you see the man at the flower table?
Yes. Is he buying those yellow flowers?
Yes, that's Bill. He buys flowers for his mother every Saturday.
Who's the girl at the café? She's drinking something orange.
That's Grace. She's drinking orange juice. She's my best friend.
And that boy is buying carrots from the man at the vegetable table.
Hugo. He's buying vegetables for his mother's soup.
Now listen to Part One again.
p2: Part Two. Listen and look. There is one example.
Mum, when is the market? On Friday?
No, the market is on Saturday. Every week.
Saturday. OK, I'm writing it down.
Can you see the answer? Now you listen and write.
Buy the bread from the woman at the second table. Her name is Mrs Baker.
Baker? Like the person who makes bread?
Yes! B-A-K-E-R. It's a funny name for her, isn't it?
How many oranges do we need?
Fourteen, please. Seven for the juice and seven for your lunch boxes.
Fourteen oranges. That's a lot of juice!
No, for Grandma. It's her birthday on Monday.
Flowers for Grandma. She loves the red ones.
What time does the market close?
At two o'clock. Don't be late or the tables aren't there!
Two o'clock. I can go at eleven.
And your father is going to the market too. Meet him there.
Where? Next to the bread table?
No, next to the café. He always drinks a coffee there.
Now listen to Part Two again.
p3: Part Three. Listen and look. There is one example.
Hugo is telling his teacher what his family bought at the market. What did each person buy?
Hugo, did you go to the market on Saturday?
Yes! I bought bananas because I have one every day after school.
Can you see the letter A? Now you listen and write a letter in each box.
And your mother? What did she buy?
She bought tomatoes. Lots of them. She's making a big salad for Sunday lunch.
He bought a jacket! It's blue and it wasn't expensive. His old one was very old.
Yes, flowers for her bedroom. She puts them next to her bed.
And your uncle? He was with you, wasn't he?
Yes. He bought cheese. He eats cheese with everything, even with cake!
She bought bread from Mrs Baker. It was hot and we ate some in the street.
Now listen to Part Three again.
p4: Part Four. Look at the pictures. Listen and look. There is one example.
I need eggs, milk and rice. What do I buy first?
Buy the milk first, because the shop closes early.
OK, milk first. Then the eggs and the rice.
Can you see the tick? Now you listen and tick the box.
One. Which fruit did Grandma buy?
No, the apples were very small this week. I bought grapes.
Peter, do you want a bag for the potatoes?
No, thank you. I’ve got this box. My bag is at home.
The box is very big, you know.
Three. Which fruit doesn’t Grace like?
I love oranges and I love grapes.
What about pears? Shall I buy some?
No, thank you. I don’t like pears.
Four. Where is the flower table?
Excuse me, where are the flowers, please?
They’re at the end, next to the café.
No, next to the café. You can see them from here.
Five. What is the weather like at the market?
Hold it! It’s very windy today.
No, there’s no rain today. Only wind.
Now listen to Part Four again.
p5: Part Five. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Here’s a picture of a market table. Can you see the bag of potatoes under the table?
Can you see the brown bag? This is an example. Now you listen and colour and write.
Now, can you see the bird on the roof?
There’s a cat next to the box. Can I colour it?
Can you see the carrots on the table?
Colour them green. I know, that’s a funny colour for carrots!
Yes. There’s a small board on the table with nothing on it. Write the word ‘fruit’. F-R-U-I-T.
And now the box with the apples in it. Colour the box yellow.
Well done. That’s a very colourful market.
Now listen to Part Five again.
